To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the magnet temperature can be estimated with a worst case error less that 10 K, the thermal expansion can be taken into account, the fundamental wave model is valid at low speeds and standstill and the fundamental wave model quantities can be estimated in real time within one switching cycle.
A permanent magnet temperature observer based on the electrical fundamental wave model quantities is a powerful method to prevent irreversible magnet demagnetization.
a model-based permanent magnet temperature observer is feasible and can be used in real applications.
In summary, our research is concerned with
an accurate and robust estimation of the temperature of the permanent magnets in permanent magnet synchronous motors.
the development and validation of an exact flux linkage estimator for the estimation of the permanent magnet temperature.
a novel, sensorless permanent-magnet temperature observer for electrical drives.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed observer is suitable to monitor the permanent magnet temperature in a real-world application.
the proposed permanent magnet temperature observer is a promising approach for a wide range of applications.
the presented method is a promising candidate for permanent-magnet temperature estimation in synchronous motors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
it is possible to estimate the permanent magnet temperature of synchronous motors based on electrical fundamental wave quantities.
the proposed observer is able to accurately estimate the magnet temperature of a permanent magnet synchronous machine in all operation points, even at low speeds or standstill.
the observer is able to track the temperature of the magnet with a high precision, even at very low speed or standstill.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a fundamental wave observer for the magnet temperature of synchronous machines is feasible and applicable in practice.

a simple model-based observer is able to provide a reliable temperature estimate of the permanent magnet in the presence of thermal and electrical nonlinearities, which is a prerequisite to prevent irreversible demagnetization of the rotor.
a permanent magnet temperature estimation based on the fundamental wave model quantities is possible and can be used for a wide range of operating conditions.
